import re$
$
$
_SINGLE = re.compile(r"^-?\d+$")$
$
$
_RANGE = re.compile(r"^(-?\d+)\s*-\s*(-?\d+)$")$
$
$
def parse_range(s: str) -> list[int]:$
    if s.strip() == "":$
        return []$
    out = set()$
    for token in s.split(","):$
        token = token.strip()$
        if not token:$
            raise ValueError("empty token")$
        if _SINGLE.match(token):$
            out.add(int(token))$
            continue$
        m = _RANGE.match(token)$
        if not m:$
            raise ValueError(f"bad token: {token!r}")$
        a, b = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))$
        if a > b:$
            raise ValueError(f"reversed range: {token!r}")$
        out.update(range(a, b))$
    return sorted(out)$

content.text: The cause is in `solution/core.py`: the range expansion uses `range(a, b)`, which excludes the end value. Ranges are inclusive, so it should be `range(a, b + 1)`.

content.text: The visible suite now passes (3/3). I changed one line in `solution/core.py`: the range expansion in `parse_range` used `range(a, b)`, which drops the end value of every `a-b` token, so `-3--1` produced `[-3, -2]` and `7-9` lost `9`. Ranges are inclusive, so it is now `range(a, b + 1)`. I changed nothing under `tests/`, added no dependencies, and left `solution/__init__.py` and the `parse_range` signature untouched.
